source_evidence: These classes of funds also pay 12b-1 fees, which are part of the fund’s ongoing operating expenses paid out of the fund’s assets to cover the costs of marketing and selling fund shares.
answer: A 12b-1 fee is an ongoing operating expense paid from a mutual fund’s assets to help cover the costs of marketing and selling its shares. It is separate from any sales load or transaction fee. Some no-load share classes can also have 12b-1 fees, so “no-load” does not necessarily mean there are no ongoing fees. Check the share class’s fee information to understand which costs apply.
